In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-10, z.string().toString() evaluates to '[object Object]' so the two computed schema keys collide and the schema effectively only validates access_token; the 'any numeric property is expiry' rule is a no-op and Zod strips unknown keys, so the parsed data only contains access_token plus a literal placeholder refresh_token string that can be spread into and corrupt real stored credentials (e.g. O365, Zoom)

In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16, sync mode returns a raw fetch Response which no caller can consume: Google accesses res.data and throws TypeError, Hubspot reads undefined fields and persists garbage (NaN expiry), Zoho/Zoho-Bigin access tokenInfo.data.error and throw TypeError, and Lark's handleLarkError expects a Lark envelope shape the sync response doesn't have, so all refresh flows crash or persist unusable tokens when sync is enabled

In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:93, credentialId is passed instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint looks up the wrong user and returns the wrong user's tokens, causing a silent cross-user credential mismatch

In .env.example:241-243, the key-length guidance says 32 bytes for AES-256 but the suggested command `openssl rand -base64 24` produces 24 bytes, and following the neighboring -base64 32 pattern yields a 44-byte string that createDecipheriv rejects, guiding users into an invalid encryption key

SafeParse wrapper object (full SafeParseReturnType with success/data) stored as the Google credential key in CalendarService.ts instead of .data, corrupting the key so subsequent schema validation fails and permanently breaking the user's calendar sync

The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys z.string().toString() which evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", requiring a property with that name to be a number, so sync-mode safeParse always fails and parseRefreshTokenResponse throws for every real OAuth response

Literal string "refresh_token" is persisted to the database as a placeholder when the schema strips the real refresh_token, causing the next refresh attempt to fail against the provider for adapters like Zoom and Office365 (Salesforce correctly re-merges the original token but others do not)
Hubspot's sync path returns a raw fetch Response where the caller requires a HubspotToken object, so reading expires_in yields NaN, masked by an `as HubspotToken` cast
Zoho Bigin/CRM's sync path returns a fetch Response where the caller reads tokenInfo.data.error (an axios response shape), causing TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined
Google's CalendarService reads res?.data from the sync-mode fetch Response, which does not have a data property, causing the same shape mismatch as other adapters

The new webhook endpoint app-credential.ts persists decrypted credential payloads with zero schema validation against any app-specific zod schema, allowing malformed sync payloads to corrupt credentials until re-authentication
The webhook handler has no try/catch around JSON.parse, symmetricDecrypt, or zod .parse(req.body), so malformed requests yield an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx response
The webhook endpoint has no req.method check, so GET/PUT/DELETE requests all execute the credential write path
The outgoing sync request in refreshOAuthTokens.ts sends no authentication header (e.g., CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) to the parent app's endpoint, leaving the sync channel unauthenticated
The outgoing sync request never checks response.ok or response status, so 404/500 responses from the parent app flow silently into downstream token-parsing logic as garbage data

SalesforceCalendarService performs a network token refresh on every service instantiation with no expiry check, hammering Salesforce's token endpoint and risking rate-limiting or refresh-token invalidation

Salesforce token refresh gates success on response.statusText !== "OK", which is empty for HTTP/2 responses and unreliable on some proxies, causing valid 200 responses to be rejected with a 400 error; response.ok is the only reliable predicate

The entire diff contains zero test files, e2e specs, or fixtures for the new public webhook endpoint, feature-flag-gated token-refresh path across 8 adapters, and AES-256 credential decryption, leaving the new behavior completely unverified

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}) instead of the parsed data, so after the first Google token refresh, credentials are persisted as {success: true, data: {...}} instead of the credential object, corrupting every Google Calendar credential even with credential sharing disabled (CalendarService.ts:96)

The schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-10 uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", and the duplicate key means the numeric expiry requirement is not enforced, so in sharing mode a sync response containing only access_token passes validation and no expiry is extracted

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:23-25 fabricates a refresh_token sentinel: when refresh_token is absent (e.g., Zoom responses), the literal string "refresh_token" is written into the persisted credential, causing the next refresh to fail auth and permanently breaking the credential

refreshOAuthTokens only syncs if userId is present and the webhook schema requires userId, but createOAuthAppCredential supports team-owned credentials (userId: null), so team credentials are never synced and cannot be pushed via the webhook

Bigin passes credentialId where every other adapter passes credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint refreshes credentials for the wrong user, corrupting another user's credentials or 404ing

Salesforce code performs an unconditional token refresh (network call to Salesforce + prisma.credential.update) on every construction of SalesforceCalendarService with no expiry check, hitting Salesforce rate limits and adding latency to every booking-page check

Salesforce's refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely, contradicting the PR's architecture, and in sharing mode zod strips unknown keys so instance_url, signature, and id are wiped from the stored credential, destroying fields jsforce.Connection needs while the parent app's copy diverges

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:7-10 uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", and the duplicate key means the numeric expiry requirement is not enforced, so in sharing mode a sync response containing only access_token passes validation and no expiry is extracted

adjudication_records.issue_text: In sharing mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse strips expires_in/expiry_date from the parent-app response in Office365 (and Zoom), so the stored expiry is never updated and a token refresh fires on every API call, creating an unbounded refresh loop on the booking hot path

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens writes the sentinel string 'refresh_token' into the credential whenever the response lacks a refresh token, and this sentinel is persisted via prisma.credential.update, breaking the credential if sharing is disabled or any unwrapped path refreshes directly

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show `refreshOAuthTokens` writing any sentinel into credentials; it only chooses between calling a remote sync endpoint vs the normal refresh function. However, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` *does* forcibly set `refresh_token` to the string "refresh_token" when missing (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`). adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(...)` (a raw `Response`) (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts:21-26 has header-name case sensitivity and non-constant-time secret comparison issues

adjudication.rationale:
In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret is validated via a direct string inequality check:

```ts
req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
```

1) Header-name case sensitivity: in Node/Next, `req.headers` keys are normalized to lowercase. This code uses the env-provided header name verbatim as the lookup key; if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is set with any uppercase characters, the lookup will fail and reject valid requests. The comment says it "should be in lowercase", but the implementation does not enforce it, so the defect is present in the diff.

2) Non-constant-time comparison: comparing secrets with `!==` is not constant-time and can theoretically leak information via timing differences. The diff shows no constant-time compare (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`), so the issue is real and security-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook secret in app-credential.ts is compared with !== (non-constant-time) on an unauthenticated public endpoint with no rate limiting, creating a timing oracle for byte-by-byte recovery of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual

That means in sharing mode Hubspot will receive a `Response` instead of a `HubspotToken`, causing response-as-token type confusion and likely breaking downstream token handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken computed-key zod schema where [z.string().toString()] collapses to "[object Object]" (deferred)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Since `z.string()` returns a Zod schema object, calling `.toString()` on it yields a literal string like `"[object Object]"`, so the object shape ends up with a single fixed key rather than a dynamic/index signature. This both collapses/overwrites keys and does not achieve the intended "any numeric expiry field" / "allow other properties" behavior, making the schema effectively broken and likely rejecting/accepting wrong responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook auth-header edge cases (deferred: functional/security concern)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the auth check compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` directly to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next.js/Node, `req.headers[...]` is typed as `string | string[] | undefined`; if the header is present multiple times (or parsed as an array), the comparison will fail even when the secret is included, causing valid webhook requests to be rejected. Additionally, the lookup assumes the env-provided header name matches Node’s lowercased header keys (they only comment this, not enforce it), which can also cause false 403s.
